# Incident Report — 2024-09-04 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host
| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 172.17.0.99 | Source of all C2 traffic; conversation table |
| MAC | 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4 | ARP (`arp.src.proto_ipv4==172.17.0.99`) and Ethernet frames to/from 172.17.0.99 |
| Hostname | DESKTOP-RNVO9AT | DHCP option 12 (`dhcp.option.hostname`), NBNS `<00>`/`<20>` records, DNS queries for `DESKTOP-RNVO9AT.bepositive.com` |
| AD domain / NetBIOS | bepositive.com / BEPOSITIVE | DNS SRV queries (`_ldap._tcp...bepositive.com`), NBNS `BEPOSITIVE<00>/<1e>` |
| Logged-in user | afletcher | Kerberos `CNameString` field on AS-REQ/TGS-REQ exchanges between 172.17.0.99 and DC 172.17.0.17 |
| Domain controller | 172.17.0.17 (WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19, MAC 00:23:ae:50:ba:fd) | NBNS `<20>` Server service, LDAP/Kerberos/DHCP source |

## Malware Family
**Win32/Koi Stealer** — **signature-confirmed**. The provided Suricata/IDS alert export contains rule hit `ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin (POST) M2` (48 hits, first seen 2024-09-04 17:35 UTC) firing on 172.17.0.99 → 79.124.78.197:80. This is independently corroborated in the pcap: 96 nearly-periodic `POST /foots.php` requests from 172.17.0.99 to 79.124.78.197, each with `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`, `Content-Encoding: binary`, a spoofed legacy User-Agent (`Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; Windows NT 10.0; ...)`), and small encrypted/opaque bodies tagged with a persistent client GUID `30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654` — a classic stealer beacon/checkin pattern, matching the "GENERIC SUSPICIOUS POST to Dotted Quad with Fake Browser" alert also present in the alert file.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint**
- `79.124.78.197:80` — destination of all `/foots.php` and `/index.php` HTTP requests from the victim; bare-IP `Host:` header (no domain), matching both the IDS alert and the observed beacon traffic in `tcp.stream 48/51/56` etc.

**URLs (grounded in `http.request` traffic to 79.124.78.197)**
- `http://79.124.78.197/foots.php` — repeated POST checkin, ~96 occurrences from t+155s through t+3576s (roughly every 90–120s over the life of the capture)
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` — GET, response body contains `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn|qIOuKk7U|http://79.124.78.197/index.php|`
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php` — follow-up POST with encrypted binary body (105 bytes)

**Domain**
- None grounded. The C2 was contacted by bare IP with no corresponding DNS lookup in the capture — consistent with the "Dotted Quad" IDS alert.

**File names / SHA256 hashes**
- None observed. `--export-objects http` over the full capture yields no executable, script, or archive with recoverable content — only tiny stub artifacts (Microsoft connect-test text, a 4-byte Adobe `ProcessMAU.txt`, and the empty/near-empty stealer POST/response bodies). The stealer's exfil payloads are opaque encrypted blobs inside POST bodies, not named file transfers, so no file name or hash can be grounded to this capture.

## Benign Context (not indicators)
- 172.17.0.17 (DC), all AD/Kerberos/LDAP/SMB/NBNS traffic to it — normal domain-joined workstation behavior. The GPL NETBIOS/SMBv1/Kerberos-overflow alerts in the alert file all fire on this DC traffic and read as legacy-signature false positives on ordinary AD authentication, not lateral movement.
- Microsoft telemetry/services: `www.msftconnecttest.com`, `*.events.data.microsoft.com`, `login.microsoftonline.com`, `officeclient.microsoft.com`, `odc.officeapps.live.com`, `ctldl.windowsupdate.com`, `client.wns.windows.com`, `ecs.office.com`
- Consumer/browser noise: `www.bing.com`, `th.bing.com`, `www.msn.com`, `assets.msn.com`, `img-s-msn-com.akamaized.net`, `weathermapdata.blob.core.windows.net`, `g.live.com`
- `acroipm2.adobe.com` (Adobe update check), `x1.c.lencr.org` (Let's Encrypt OCSP), `sso.godaddy.com`
- `www.bellantonicioccolato.it` (46.254.34.201) — a TLS session to this Italian bakery site opens ~2 seconds before the first Koi Stealer checkin. Timing is suggestive of it being part of the delivery/redirect chain, but the session is TLS-encrypted with no visible content, so it is **not** asserted as a confirmed IOC here.

## Incident Summary
The Windows workstation **DESKTOP-RNVO9AT** (172.17.0.99, MAC 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4), logged in as domain user **afletcher** on the `bepositive.com` AD domain, was infected with **Win32/Koi Stealer** (signature-confirmed via ETPRO rule). Starting at 17:35 UTC the host began beaconing to C2 **79.124.78.197:80**, repeatedly POSTing encrypted binary data to `/foots.php` under a spoofed IE7 user-agent and a fixed client GUID, continuing for the entire ~1-hour duration of the capture. No executable or exfiltrated file was recoverable from the capture in cleartext, so no file names or hashes can be reported; the initial infection vector is not conclusively captured, though a TLS session to `www.bellantonicioccolato.it` immediately preceding the first C2 checkin is a plausible but unconfirmed delivery-chain link.
